- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to recognize; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; use 7-day rolling average to dampen noise before forecasting.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.33, -0.50, +0.33), model may misalign with trend; align forecast to sentiment median rather than peak.
